messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty triggered: severity P1 -> infra.az8.region_capacity_alert. Symptoms: sustained 500s from eu-west-az8 serving tier, token queues growing on nodes handling model-shard-12. Runbook ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-capacity-evac

PagerDuty: alert auto-retries=3, paging Emma (oncall)

Emma (oncall): acked via PD. I'm on it. Checking dashboards and logs.

Emma (oncall): initial triage — spike of 5xx concentrated in eu-west-az8. Embeddings paths OK. Customers reporting timeouts around 8-12s for /v1/generate calls.

Raj: infra oncall here. Pulling node metrics. Any recent deploys? Emma: none in last 3h.

SRE-Alex: joining. If autoscaler thrash, we should consider traffic diversion sooner rather than later.

Emma (oncall): proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z ERROR request_id=abc123 status=502 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-large shard=12 upstream_timeout
2026-03-15T10:12:35Z WARN kvcache evicted=2400 shard=12
```

Raj: kubelets flapping on ~6 nodes in infer-gpu-pool-3; seeing OOM kills and node pressure events.

Chris: routing infra here. Can we run a canary divert to az5 in-region?

Emma (oncall): yes. Plan: canary 20% -> az5, monitor errors and latency, then escalate to 50/50 if stable.

SRE-Alex: agreed. I'll prepare routing change. Chris, ready to apply when I give the go.

PagerDuty: escalation to Level 2 (SRE-Alex) due to sustained errors and >5min ack window.

Emma (oncall): applying canary now. Notifying CS.

Chris: executing:
```
internal-router set-weight --route /v1/generate --from az8=80 az5=20 --reason 'eu-west-az8 node pressure 2026-03-15'
```

Maya (Customer Success): informed affected customers: "We've diverted a portion of traffic to reduce errors; expected visible improvement in 10-15 minutes. We'll follow up with full incident report." :email:

Emma (oncall): canary metrics after 8m: az5 error rate 0.6%, p95 220ms; az8 down from ~28% to 11% and trending down. Queue depth falling.

Raj: node churn slowed; OOMs decreased. Hypothesis: sudden KV-cache churn on shard-12 amplified by a recent kernel driver memory accounting change.

SRE-Alex: prepare to move to 50% if recovery doesn't reach <2% 5xx within 15m. Also schedule rolling reboot on affected nodes to clear the kernel state — one at a time.

Emma (oncall): agreed. Also note: warming strategy needed post-failover to avoid cold-cache spikes.

Chris: increasing to 50%
```
internal-router set-weight --route /v1/generate --from az8=50 az5=50 --reason 'canary success: ramp to continue migration'
```

Raj: starting node reboot sequence with drain/cordon, 5m wait between reboots:
```
kubectl drain node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n redwood-serving
ssh node-xyz sudo reboot
kubectl uncordon node-xyz
```

SRE-Alex: enable temporary higher retry budgets where safe, and watch token-buckets and client-side circuit breakers.

Emma (oncall): metrics now: az8 5xx ~3.2%, p95 improving. If <2% in 10m we can either return to az8 primary or keep az5 as primary for post-incident stability.

Maya (Customer Success): posting customer update: "We've diverted traffic and are performing maintenance; expected resolution within 15 minutes. Will follow with RCA." :handshake:

20m later

Emma (oncall): az8 dropped below 1.7% 5xx. Node reboots completed and report healthy. Recommend shifting traffic back gradually.

SRE-Alex: agree. Rolling back weights.

Chris:
```
internal-router set-weight --route /v1/generate --from az8=95 az5=5 --reason 'az8 recovered'
internal-router set-weight --route /v1/generate --from az8=100 az5=0 --reason 'complete recovery'
```

PagerDuty: incident marked resolved. Timeline: fired -> ack (Emma) -> escalated -> canary -> ramp -> node reboots -> resolved.

Emma (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall (Chris): watch KV-cache evictions for shard-12 and kernel driver changes on node images; follow runbook az-capacity-evac. I'll open a postmortem doc and tag infra-release for a potential kernel driver revert.

SRE-Alex: creating follow-ups: (1) investigate kernel driver memory accounting, (2) add prefix warmup on failover, (3) adjust autoscaler thresholds for GPU pools.

Maya (Customer Success): will update tickets and notify customers when postmortem link is available.

Emma (oncall): handing off at 11:10 UTC to Chris. All alerts are quiet. Will post the postmortem in this channel when ready.

Chris: taking handoff — dashboards steady. Monitoring evictions for next hour.

IncidentBot: Thread closed by Emma (oncall).
